AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Pancreatolithiasis occurs in less than 1% of the general population and is mainly recognized in patients with chronic pancreatitis. Selection of the appropriate treatment method depends on location, size and number of stones.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: The aim of the study was to analyze the data concerning patients with pancreatic duct stones who were hospitalized in the Department of Gastroenterology and Hepatology in years 2010-2014.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: The study presents the data on 16 patients with pancreatic duct stones that constituted 7% of all 228 patients with chronic pancreatitis hospitalized in the Department in that period. The own clinical material was compared with literature data.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Epigastric pain was the most common symptom reported by the patients with pancreatolithiasis. The sensitivity of imaging tests in the diagnosis of pancreatic duct stones was as follow: abdominal ultrasonography - 31%, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) - 67%, computed tomography - 71%, endoscopic ultrasonography - 73%. In 6 patients ERCP and sphincterotomy was performed together with the main pancreatic duct stenting. Three other subjects were qualified for surgical treatment. In the case of seven patients conservative treatment and further observation were applied.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Endoscopic ultrasonography is characterized by a high sensitivity in the diagnosis of pancreatic duct stones. ERCP is the first-line treatment in the case of a small number of stones, with size below 5 mm, and located in the head or body of the pancreas. In the case of stones with size ≥ 5 mm extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy should be performed before the endoscopic drainage during ERCP. The stenosis of the main pancreatic duct is the key risk factor of the recurrence of pancreatolithiasis.
